title: 1950201-PPM-001
summary:
- The document is titled 'MAGNETIC PARTICLES PROCEDURE' and is owned by Abengoa.
- It outlines the procedure for Magnetic Particle Testing in welded joints, edges, and metallic material of a project.
- The procedure requires qualified personnel at least as Level 2 to evaluate indications.
- The document references ASME Code, Section V and other standards for non-destructive examination.
- There is a revision history detailing updates to the procedure.
- The procedure requires requalification for essential variable changes and revision for all other changes.
- Equipment includes AC yoke with a pull force of 4.5 kg and UV-A lamp with specific wavelength and intensity.
- Wet particles must be fluorescent or non-fluorescent, while dry particles require specific temperature limits.
- Examination involves applying magnetic particles on the surface, using continuous method for both wet and dry particles.
- Field strength must be checked with a Berthol sample to ensure appropriate magnetizing field.
- Multiple magnetic fields should be applied to guarantee 100% coverage of the surface.
- The procedure involves magnetic particle examination for detecting surface and subsurface discontinuities in welds and components.
summary_points: The document is titled 'MAGNETIC PARTICLES PROCEDURE' and is owned by Abengoa.
It outlines the procedure for Magnetic Particle Testing in welded joints, edges, and metallic material of a project.
The procedure requires qualified personnel at least as Level 2 to evaluate indications.
The document references ASME Code, Section V and other standards for non-destructive examination.
There is a revision history detailing updates to the procedure.
The procedure requires requalification for essential variable changes and revision for all other changes.
Equipment includes AC yoke with a pull force of 4.5 kg and UV-A lamp with specific wavelength and intensity.
Wet particles must be fluorescent or non-fluorescent, while dry particles require specific temperature limits.
Examination involves applying magnetic particles on the surface, using continuous method for both wet and dry particles.
Field strength must be checked with a Berthol sample to ensure appropriate magnetizing field.
Multiple magnetic fields should be applied to guarantee 100% coverage of the surface.
The procedure involves magnetic particle examination for detecting surface and subsurface discontinuities in welds and components.
Indications with major dimensions greater than 1.5 mm are considered relevant.
Acceptance criteria include specific types of cracks, linear and rounded indications, and their sizes.
Final reports must document job number, procedure details, drawing, and evaluation results.
Requirements for the procedure include magnetizing technique, particle application, and equipment qualification.
El procedimiento incluye equipos específicos para la magnetización y inspección por partículas magnéticas.
Se utilizan partículas húmedas y secas con diferentes características según las condiciones de temperatura.
La inspección se realiza mediante el método de campo continuo, aplicando partículas en la superficie de la pieza.
Es necesario comprobar la intensidad del campo magnético con un indicador tipo cruz de Berthol.
Se requiere una limpieza final antes de continuar con los siguientes procesos.
El procedimiento incluye evaluación y criterios de aceptación para partículas magnéticas.
Se consideran relevantes indicaciones con dimensiones superiores a 1.5 mm.
Las superficies examinadas deben estar libres de grietas y indicaciones redondas mayores de ciertos tamaños.
El informe final debe incluir detalles como número de trabajo, procedimiento, plano y resultados de la inspección.
